title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this continuation of La Longue Marche (1981), an 'L-group' is a discrete group carrying an 'L-structure'. This is most likely Grothendieck's 'groupe à lacets': a surface-type group together with its distinguished conjugacy classes of peripheral loops ('lacets') and orientation data. The previous page shows two things. First, π ↦ L(π) is functorial for outer isomorphisms. Second, for an extension 1→π0→π→G→1 with G finite, L-structures on π correspond to L-structures on π0 that are invariant under the outer action G=π/π0→Out(π0). The standard example is a surface X of finite type, a finite group G acting on X, and the equivariant (orbifold) fundamental group π=π1(X,G;a), giving 1→π1(X,a)→π→G→1.

This page:
(1) The canonical L-structure of π0=π1(X,a) is invariant under the outer action of G, so Π=π1(X,G;a) inherits an L-structure.
(2) Grothendieck conjectures that every L-group is isomorphic to one obtained this way. He calls this 'deep', essentially equivalent to the existence of fixed points of finite subgroups of Teichmüller modular groups acting on Teichmüller space, and 'not totally understood'. That fixed-point statement is the Nielsen realization problem. An abstract finite extension of a surface group with prescribed outer action is geometrically realized iff the finite subgroup of the mapping class group fixes a point of Teichmüller space.
(3) Programme: find a 'good general statement' relating two 2-categories. One is the 2-category of L-groups, with outer isomorphisms as arrows. The other is that of surfaces of finite type carrying a positive divisor d with finite support, weighted in N*. To each such pair one associates π1(X,d,a), the orbifold fundamental group with cone points of order d_i (generators γ_i with γ_i^{d_i}=1), with base point a outside supp d. This is an equivalence between 2-orbifolds (weighted surfaces) and their orbifold groups with peripheral/cone structure.
(4) Outside a few 'trivial' cases, an L-group Π≅π1(X;G,a) should be one where G acts faithfully. The next page translates this intrinsically: the centralizer of every finite-index subgroup of Π is trivial, i.e. Π has no nontrivial finite normal subgroup. The general case is then to be handled by a gluing ('recollement') step: extensions of such 'faithful' L-groups by finite groups. Finally, the link with 'L-Galois topoi' is to be made, paraphrasing the theory of Galois topoi of discrete groups.

Purpose: build a combinatorial/group-theoretic model, in the 2-category of outer groups, for the 'geometric' objects (surfaces with marked points and weights, i.e. orbifold curves). This underlies the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) studied in La Longue Marche.
errors: The conjecture 'every L-group is obtained this way' needs hypotheses that the page only hints at: finite extension of a surface group of negative Euler characteristic, and no finite normal subgroup. Grothendieck flags the trivial/exceptional cases and the faithfulness condition himself on this page and the next.

If G contains orientation-reversing elements, the relevant fixed-point statement is for the extended mapping class group, and the realization is by NEC rather than Fuchsian groups. Whether L-structures include orientation decides which version is meant; this is unclear from the page.

The claim was not open in the strong sense he suggests. Kerckhoff announced the solution of the Nielsen realization problem in 1980 (Bull. AMS), published in Annals 1983. Zieschang and others had earlier treated the cyclic/solvable cases and the algebraic reduction. So 'not totally understood' reflects Grothendieck's information in 1981, not the state of the art.

ideas.what: L-structure on a finite extension of a surface group, induced from a G-invariant L-structure on the finite-index surface subgroup; the orbifold group π1(X,G;a) of a finite group action as the basic example
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group / peripheral structure on virtual surface groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds, 1978-80); classical Fuchsian/NEC group theory (Fricke-Klein, Macbeath, Zieschang)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated; 'groupes à lacets'); Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the discrete/profinite Teichmüller groupoids

ideas.what: Realizing every L-group as an orbifold group is essentially equivalent to finite subgroups of Teichmüller modular groups having fixed points on Teichmüller space
ideas.modern_name: Nielsen realization problem and its algebraic equivalent (finite extensions of surface groups are Fuchsian/NEC)
ideas.where_published: possibly in the circulated parts of La Longue Marche; not in Esquisse as far as I know

ideas.what: Proposed 2-categorical equivalence between L-groups (outer isomorphisms) and surfaces of finite type with weighted positive divisors of finite support, via X ↦ π1(X,d,a)
ideas.modern_name: equivalence between hyperbolic 2-orbifolds and Fuchsian groups with peripheral structure, as 2-categories/stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Fenchel-Nielsen, Zieschang-Vogt-Coldewey 'Surfaces and planar discontinuous groups'); 2-categorical/stacky phrasing in anabelian literature (Nakamura, Mochizuki on orbicurves, Hoshi-Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: related ideas in La Longue Marche and Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Faithfulness of G expressed intrinsically: the centralizer of every finite-index subgroup of Π is trivial; the general case is obtained by extensions by finite groups
ideas.modern_name: no finite normal subgroups / 'slim' groups (Mochizuki's terminology) ; gerbes over orbifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki ('slim' profinite groups), classical group theory

ideas.what: Plan to relate L-groups to 'L-Galois topoi', by analogy with Galois topoi of discrete groups
ideas.modern_name: classifying topos / orbifold-stack topos with peripheral (log) structure
ideas.where_published: Galois topoi in SGA4 / Longue Marche

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly links his algebraic notion of L-group (a group with loop structure) to the Nielsen realization problem. He sees the realization of every L-group as an orbifold group as essentially equivalent to fixed points of finite subgroups of Teichmüller groups. This is an independent identification of a known equivalence (Zieschang/Kerckhoff), made inside the anabelian programme.
missed.quote: c'est là un résultat qui semble profond (esst. équivalent à celui de l'existence des pts fixes des sous-groupes finis des groupes de Teichmüller ...), et qui n'est pas compris totalement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows that in 1981 Grothendieck viewed Nielsen realization as a foundational input for the discrete side of the Teichmüller tower. The equivalence itself is known in the literature.

missed.claim: He asks for a 'good general statement': a 2-categorical equivalence between L-groups and weighted punctured surfaces, including non-faithful cases via finite extensions (gluing), and an 'L-Galois topos' version.
missed.quote: Il faudrait dégager un "bon énoncé" général, reliant la 2-catégorie des L-groupes, avec celle des surfaces de caractère fini, pondérées
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Discrete orbifold-group/stack equivalences are standard. A clean published 2-categorical statement in Grothendieck's 'groupe à lacets' language, including finite gerbes and the topos version, is not something I can point to. It is close to, but not identical with, statements in combinatorial anabelian geometry (Hoshi-Mochizuki).

deep.surprise_reason: The page independently recognizes the equivalence of the group-theoretic realization problem with Nielsen realization, and sketches a 2-categorical orbifold/L-group dictionary. Interesting historically, but the mathematics (Kerckhoff 1983, Fuchsian/NEC group theory, orbifold stacks) is established in the literature.

'Π' and 'π' are used interchangeably for the same group; likely 'un L-groupe Π'.
'esst. équivalent à celui des l'existence des pts fixes': the insertion reads 'à celui de l'existence des pts fixes des sous-groupes finis des groupes de Teichmüller'.
'Il faudrait dégager un "bon énoncé" général': 'dégager' is inserted above, apparently replacing a crossed-out word.

'relatif à un pt base a ∈ X − supp d' (d underlined, as a divisor).
